question: How many different positive three-digit integers can be formed using only the digits in the set $\{2, 3, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6\}$ if no digit may be used more times than it appears in the given set of available digits?
solution:
Classify the integers by how many distinct digits they use. None of the available digits is zero, so every allowed ordering gives a three-digit integer.
Three distinct digits: using 2, 3, 5, and 6 as choices, there are 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 ordered triples without repetition.
Two distinct digits: the repeated digit must be 5 or 6 (2 choices). The other digit can be any of the remaining 3 digits and can occupy any of 3 positions, giving 2 × 3 × 3 = 18 integers.
One distinct digit: only 5 appears at least three times, so only 555 qualifies.
The total is 24 + 18 + 1 = 43.
Final answer: 43
